requirements.text: If the article is currently published, its short description will be minimally updated to include the notation " - Updated International Payment Guidance."

body: LIKE 'Common payroll questions and answers including paycheck timing, deductions, and tax forms.%'

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 3 AND body LIKE 'Common payroll questions and answers including paycheck timing, deductions, and tax forms.%' AND body LIKE '% - Updated International Payment Guidance.'
assumptions: the Payroll FAQ is knowledge_id 3 (KB-003), the only article of that title, and it is published, so the update branch applies
the knowledge table has no short description column; body kept from the benchmark check as the column that carries it
'minimally updated to include' read as appending the notation to the existing body, so the original opening text remains

disagreement: body prefix: A LIKE 'Common payroll questions and answers%', B LIKE the whole seed body followed by '%'; chose B's because both are right and B's is tighter: a minimal update that appends the notation keeps the entire seed body, which is exactly that sentence

requirements.text: If the crucial "Payroll Expert" skill is found to be absent from his profile ... The necessary capability is added to his professional record
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_skill WHERE user_skill_id = 9 AND skill = 3 AND user = 2
assumptions: Michael Rodriguez is user 2 (michael.rodriguez@techcorp.com), the only user of that name
Payroll Expert is skill 3; Michael's only skill is Performance Management, so the absent branch applies

requirements.text: he is subsequently assigned a high-priority task titled "Mandatory Training: Remote Performance Management."

cells.parent_case: IN (SELECT hr_case_id FROM hr_case WHERE priority = 'high')

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_task WHERE hr_case_task_id = 6 AND assigned_to = 2 AND short_description = 'Mandatory Training: Remote Performance Management' AND parent_case IN (SELECT hr_case_id FROM hr_case WHERE priority = 'high')
assumptions: tasks carry no priority column, so 'high-priority' is tested on the parent case's priority, as the benchmark check does
the request names no parent case for this branch; any high-priority parent case satisfies it

requirements.text: If the skill is confirmed to be present, he will be assigned a low-priority administrative task titled "Review Digital Nomad Policy"
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case_task WHERE short_description LIKE '%Review Digital Nomad Policy%'
assumptions: Michael lacks Payroll Expert on the seed, so the request's present-skill branch does not apply and its task must not be created

disagreement: selector: A short_description LIKE '%Review Digital Nomad Policy%', B short_description = 'Review Digital Nomad Policy'; chose A's because both are right and A's is tighter for a count that must stay at zero (it also catches a prefixed or suffixed title)

requirements.text: A new survey, designated as "Q1 Manager Remote Feedback," is created ... The survey includes a key evaluative question

cells.question_5: To what extent do you feel your manager trusts you to work autonomously without micromanagement?

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM survey WHERE survey_id = 3 AND question_5 = 'To what extent do you feel your manager trusts you to work autonomously without micromanagement?'
assumptions: question slot 5 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
the survey table has no name column, so 'Q1 Manager Remote Feedback' has no cell

requirements.text: a personalized instance of the survey is prepared and sent directly to him
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM survey_instance WHERE survey_instance_id = 2 AND survey_id = 3 AND assigned_to = 2
assumptions: Michael (user 2) is active on the seed, so the instance is sent
survey 3 is the newly created survey

notes:
Merged from two independent passes that agree on the requirements (the Payroll FAQ body update on knowledge 3, the Payroll Expert skill for user 2 at user_skill 9, the training task at hr_case_task 6 under a high-priority case, the stay that no 'Review Digital Nomad Policy' task is created, the survey at survey_id 3 with the question in question_5, and its instance 2 for user 2) and on all four dispositions (kept); they differ on two predicates, logged below.
disagreement: value: knowledge body prefix: one pass required the body to start with 'Common payroll questions and answers', the other with the whole seed body; chose the whole seed body because both are right and it is tighter, a minimal update keeping the existing text.
disagreement: value: Digital Nomad task stay selector: one pass used LIKE '%Review Digital Nomad Policy%', the other an exact match; chose the LIKE because both are right and it is tighter for a count that must stay at zero.
Branch resolution on the seed: the Payroll FAQ (KB-003) is published, so its text is updated rather than published; Michael Rodriguez lacks Payroll Expert, so the skill is added and the high-priority training task is created, and the low-priority 'Review Digital Nomad Policy' task is not.
The article's 'short description' has no column of that name; the benchmark tests body, so body is used (the title is the other possible reading).
The coordinating case 'Policy Rollout Logistics' with account ACC-001-003 belongs to the branch that does not apply; no case of that name exists, and the seed's only case with that account number is HRC-0003, whose description does not match the name. The training task's parent case is therefore constrained only by its high priority.
The survey check is carried jointly by the survey and survey-instance requirements. The knowledge check's kb_number predicate is replaced by the anchor knowledge_id 3 (KB-003 exists once, in organisation 1; only KB-001 and KB-002 repeat, in organisation 2).
The survey's name and the article's state have no tested cell: the survey table has no name column, and the article stays published under the applicable branch. No acting user is given, so organisation cells are left out. The policy's 30-120 character rule is not tested.
